claims.content: The Customer completes checkout and payment for won auction items by choosing which items to pay for, selecting a shipping method, and selecting a payment type.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The Customer completes checkout and payment for won auction items by choosing which items to pay for, selecting a shipping method, and selecting a payment type.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: The Customer, having won auction items, chooses which of those items to pay for, selects a shipping method, and selects a payment type, thereby completing checkout and payment.
scope_contract.start_boundary: The Customer is at checkout with won auction items and is ready to complete payment for them.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The Customer has chosen the items to pay for, selected a shipping method, and selected a payment type, completing checkout and payment.
in_scope_actions: choosing which won auction items to pay for
excluded_adjacent_actions: bidding in or winning the auction
customer-service or dispute processes after checkout
variant_dimensions: which won items are selected for payment

claims.content: Customer
The Customer has won at least one auction item and has unpaid auction winnings.

The Customer has a payment method type recorded in their registration data (for example, stored credit card information, or a previously chosen default method of payment such as PayPal or Amazon Payments).
The Customer's account is not locked or under review.

The Customer, having won at least one auction item, initiates checkout and payment by clicking a checkout entry link — such as the 'pay now' link in the winner notification email, the 'Winnings Alert' link, or another link to the Returning Winners Payments page (e.g., from My Account or related pages).
The Customer chooses which won auction items to pay for from a list of won items by checking the 'Pay Now' checkbox next to each item.
The system offers the Customer a choice of shipping methods, and the Customer selects a shipping speed option (e.g., USPS Standard or Expedited) via radio buttons.
The Customer selects a checkout option by clicking one of the payment buttons (e.g., 'Check out with PayPal' or 'Check out with Amazon').
The system starts the payment process for the Customer's selected winnings.

The Customer completes the PayPal or Amazon checkout process; upon completion, the Payment Status column in the 'Items I've Won' table displays 'Paid' for items where the transaction has been successfully completed, and the Customer is returned to a Thank You page.

Diverges from Step 1: Instead of choosing won auction items from a checkout list, the Customer accepts a 2nd-Chance offer item by clicking the 'I accept, pay with my On File credit card' button in the automated email, which triggers an automated process to generate an order without further action.

Diverges from Step 1: Instead of choosing won auction items from a checkout list, the Customer accepts a 2nd-Chance offer item by clicking the 'Pay with PayPal or Amazon Payments' button in the automated email, which generates the order, loads the Sign-In page, and after signing in takes the Customer to the Returning Winners Payments Page to pay for the order.

Diverges from Step 3: For a returning Customer whose default Method of Payment is PayPal or Amazon Payments, the system routes the Customer to a page that offers a choice of shipping methods and initiates the payment process without requiring the Customer to select a checkout option.
Diverges from Step 3: When PayPal is the default Method of Payment, the system sends an email notification and the Customer must manually log into their JTV account to process payment within 7 days.
Diverges from Step 3: The Customer selects PayPal as the payment method by choosing the corresponding radio button in the 'My Payment Methods' section.

Diverges from Step 3: The Customer selects 'Credit Card' as the payment method in the 'My New Payment Method' section and enters new billing address details (Address 1, Address 2, City, State, Zip Code, Country) to complete the transaction.

Diverges from Step 3: When paying with PayPal, the Customer logs in via the email and password fields on the right side of the page using an existing PayPal account, instead of creating a new account or using Amazon.

Diverges from Step 3: When paying with PayPal, the Customer instead creates a new PayPal account by selecting 'Create a PayPal account', entering the Country (defaulted to United States), and choosing either 'Bill Me Later®' or 'Credit Card' as the payment method.

Diverges from main flow Step 3: If the Customer clicks the 'Checkout Later' button, the system grays out the page, disables all links, and displays a DIV layer warning that payment can be made within 7 days (168 hours) but unpaid orders will be cancelled after the payment window expires. Exit: the immediate checkout/payment use case terminates without payment being completed.

Diverges from main flow Step 4: If the Customer does not complete payment for won items within 7 days (168 hours) of the auction ending time, the order is cancelled and the item is placed into Hold status. Exit: use case terminates with no payment completed and the order cancelled.

Diverges from main flow Step 4: If the Customer fails to complete the payment transaction within seven days of the auction's closing date/time, the Customer's account may be suspended. Exit: use case terminates with no payment completed.

Diverges from main flow Step 4: If the Customer's default payment method is PayPal or Amazon Payments and an order remains unpaid/unresolved beyond 7 days, the system automatically locks the account and puts it into Review Status; because the order has already been cancelled, the Customer cannot unlock the account by paying. Exit: use case terminates with no payment completed and the account locked.

Following the non-payment cancellation branch (main flow Step 4): When an order is cancelled due to non-payment, the system sends an automated email to the second-place finisher offering to sell the item at the second-place finisher's last bid price. Exit: handoff to the 2nd-Chance offer process (see alternative flow).

Diverges from the 2nd-Chance offer alternative to main flow Step 1: If the Customer does not respond to the 2nd-Chance email within 72 hours after the email is sent, the item is returned to auction available inventory and rescheduled for a future auction. Exit: the 2nd-Chance checkout/payment alternative terminates without an order.

missing_aspects: payment authorization failure handling (e.g., declined card or insufficient funds) is not specified in evidence

claims.content: The 'Payment Status' column in the 'Items I've Won' table displays 'Paid' for each item for which the transaction was successfully completed.

Upon completing the Amazon or PayPal checkout process, the Customer is returned to a Thank You page that uses the global header and footer and provides a prominent link to the JTVauctions.com home page.
The Customer has successfully completed checkout and payment for the selected won auction items.

inconsistency_hints: The Trigger lists the 'Pay with PayPal or Amazon Payments' button as an initiating action, but the Main Flow places the payment-button click at step 3, after the Customer has already selected items and shipping. If the use case is triggered by that payment button, Main Flow step 1 cannot be a continuation; it would restart the flow at an earlier point.

Postcondition 3 describes a 2nd-Chance offer accepted via the 'I accept, pay with my On File credit card' button and the automatic generation of an order. The Main Flow contains no 2nd-Chance offer handling and no on-file credit card payment step; it only covers won-item selection, shipping, and PayPal/Amazon payment buttons. Therefore this postcondition is not reachable from the Main Flow as written.

The Main Flow ends with 'The system starts the payment process for the Customer's selected winnings.' Starting the payment process does not by itself reach the postconditions that checkout/payment was successfully completed, that the Customer is returned to the Thank You page, and that the Items I've Won table shows Paid status. The flow must continue through completion of the external PayPal/Amazon payment and the resulting return/confirmation state.
